title: A Pump Is a Pressure Difference

scenes.tts: An adult human holds about five litres of blood. At rest, each side of the heart pumps roughly that much every minute. So the same few litres go round again and again. How does a pump manage that? Fluid flows from higher pressure to lower. So a pump works by making a pressure difference.

scenes.tts: Take a mammal after birth. Oxygen-poor blood from the body enters the right atrium. The right ventricle pushes it to the lungs. Oxygen-rich blood returns to the left atrium. The left ventricle pushes it on to the body. Right and left mean the animal's own right and left.

scenes.tts: Now follow the left ventricle of an adult human at rest. Each valve opens when pressure behind it exceeds pressure ahead. First comes filling. Ventricular pressure is below atrial pressure, so the mitral valve is open and blood flows in. The atrium's own contraction adds the last part.
scenes.visual: Left atrium, left ventricle and aorta as boxes with yellow pressure levels; the mitral valve opens and dots flow in.
scenes.narration: Now follow the left ventricle of an adult human at rest. Each valve opens when pressure behind it exceeds pressure ahead. First comes filling. scenes.tts: Then the ventricle contracts. Its pressure rises above atrial pressure, and the mitral valve closes. But it is still below aortic pressure, so the aortic valve stays shut. Both valves are closed, so the volume cannot change. Blood cannot enter or leave. This phase is called eye so vol you mick contraction.

scenes.tts: Ventricular pressure keeps rising. When it passes aortic pressure, about eighty millimetres of mercury, the aortic valve opens and blood leaves. Both pressures peak near one hundred twenty millimetres of mercury. Then the ventricle relaxes, its pressure falls below the aorta's, and the aortic valve closes. Both valves are shut until the mitral valve opens again.

scenes.tts: So in the reading one hundred twenty over eighty, the eighty is the aorta's lowest pressure. It is not the ventricle's. The ventricle falls to a few millimetres of mercury as it fills. The right ventricle runs the same cycle against the low resistance of the lungs. It peaks near twenty-five millimetres of mercury, It ejects the same volume at a fifth of the pressure. Keep this rule. A valve opens when pressure behind it exceeds pressure ahead.
